definition.description: A blower unit for a powered air purifying respirator system.  It has been attached to a basic rubber and plastic belt.  When active and loaded with a charged battery and a filter canister, it can be paired with a prepared PAPR mask to provide excellent protection against chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear threats.

use_action.msg: You activate your %s and the fan starts to audibly whoosh.

definition.description: A cylindrical, black-finished filter canister packed with charcoal retained between dual particulate membranes, rated to protect against chemical weapons, nerve agents, biological contaminants, radioactive dust, and all manner of other unpleasant vapors or particles.  That is, though, only if you screw it into an appropriate respirator before hand and the charcoal isn't expired.
definition.//2: Intended to simulate a standard, CBRN-rated filter cartridge with a 40mm NATO thread.
definition.//3: As it turns out, protecting your lungs from sucking down toxins is expensive.

definition.description: A light battery cell, universally compatible with all kinds of industrial-grade equipment and portable tools - drills, angle grinders, chainsaws.
A plastic test-tube housing a fluorescent purple string of unknown material.  The string gently flickers and twitches on its own.

A medium battery cell, wildly used in modern tools: heavy flashlights, two-way radios, security cameras, multiple of them make a tool battery, and some older generation of EV use thousands of this as the power storage.

A lightweight, form-fitting mask that straps over your mouth and nose.  The mask has pre-installed tubing which attaches to a powered air purifying respirator system.  Once activated it will comfortably protect against chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear threats.  Like a standard gas mask it must be prepared before use; unlike a standard gas mask, it will only function when paired with an active PAPR blower unit.  Safety goggles are advised!

definition.//: Predecessor of, and lab equivalent to, the phase immersion suit
definition.description: A bulky hazardous materials handling suit.  This one appears outfitted for the highest levels of protection, featuring built in oversized rubber gloves, sealed boot covers with a rubber sole, and an active temperature control system.  It's clearly designed to accommodate additional equipment, including self-contained breathing apparatuses or powered air purifying respirator systems.  Strange wiring snakes the entire garment, connecting to small electronic pads on all of the joints and the head.  A battery compartment marked with "X.E.D.R.A PROTOTYPE S02a" is attached to the back.

armor.//: not in direct contact with eye or mouth
feet have boot-covers with a tough footpad
standard hazmat suit on most of body

use_action.need_charges_msg: It seems like this device needs power.

definition.description: A single-piece brown and orange environmental suit, tailored in a way that slightly recalls a military flight suit.  The letters "X.E.D.R.A" are inscribed on its back, and a white shoulder patch on the right arm shows an arrow reaching within rings of concentric circles.  It requires a separate gas mask for full protection.

use_action.msg: You slip out of the top of the suit and tie the sleeves around your waist.

definition.description: Some free-floating battery charge.  It can be reloaded into rechargeable battery cells, but can never be unloaded.
definition.//: Setting battery volume to 0 causes weirdness in vehicle tests.  Please don't do that.
definition.//2: 1 battery is 1 kJ of energy. 40 batteries is an alkaline C-cell.

definition.description: A small amount of coal-derived carbon material with many small pores, used for the adsorption of harmful chemicals.  Most commonly employed within respirator filters, it traps and retains chemical gases and vapor contaminants while allowing filtered air to pass unhindered.  Once all the carbon has been bonded to intruding chemicals, the filter is expired and must be replaced.
definition.//: Obviously, activated carbon isn't magically weightless, but it's used as ammunition within gas mask filters, and the filters shouldn't equally magically grow lighter as the coal binds with chemicals. Considering that this is never found beyond gas mask canisters, having zero weight should make no difference to the player.

definition.description: An active blower unit for a powered air purifying respirator system.  It has been attached to a basic rubber and plastic belt.  If paired with a prepared PAPR mask, this will provide excellent protection against chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear threats.  The fan is audibly blowing.
A heavy battery cell, universally compatible with all kinds of industrial-grade equipment and portable tools - drills, angle grinders, chainsaws.
definition.//: Li-ion 18V LXT BL1850B by Makita, because, you guess it, there is no single standard for this type of batteries irl
Should be substantially more difficult to repair than ordinary plastic - ch_steel is difficulty 7
definition.description: An impermeable whole-body garment worn as protection against hazardous materials.  Restrictive and fragile, wearing it will provide complete protection against ambient radiation.  It requires a separate gas mask for full protection.

A bulky hazardous materials handling suit.  This one appears outfitted for the highest levels of protection, featuring built in oversized rubber gloves, sealed boot covers with a rubber sole, and an active temperature control system.  It's clearly designed to accommodate additional equipment, including self-contained breathing apparatuses or powered air purifying respirator systems.  Strange wiring snakes the entire garment, connecting to small electronic pads on all of the joints and the head.  A battery compartment marked with "X.E.D.R.A PROTOTYPE S02a" is attached to the back.  The device is currently switched on.

A lightweight environmental suit incorporating Kevlar-lined boots and gloves, worn by Hub personnel in their rare forays aboveground.  Colored brown and blue, the white seal of Hub 01 is embroidered on both of its upper arms.  It requires a separate gas mask for full protection.
definition.//: 2mm Nomex across the entire suit with a waterproof silicone outer to provide hazmat properties. Hands and feet reinforced/shaped with other materials to provide full-body hazmat protection with minimal encumbrance.

material.//: Back of hand from the wrist to the knuckles can be stiffer but still needs a little flexibility. This area can afford the most thickness on gloves.
Molded knuckle plates, spacious enough inside the gloves to flex your knuckles fine while providing extra knuckle protection because busting your knuckles sucks.
A bit of Kevlar between the third and second knuckles, the part of the fingers where flexibility is least important.
Fingers need to be the most flexible and tactile part of the hand. Lycra/nylon blend (as the lycra material is defined) will give both those qualities while sacrificing the least protection.
The boots are reinforced with plastic plates throughout to protect against penetration.
The Kevlar is 2mm thick over most of the boots, and 1mm thick for flexible joints.
Steel shank for excellent arch support and to maintain boot shape for longevity.

use_action.msg: You slip out of the top of the suit and tie the sleeves around your waist.

definition.description: A single-piece brown and orange environmental suit, tailored in a way that slightly recalls a military flight suit.  The upper portion has been tied around the waist casually.
